original_acceptance_criteria: a definition containing a TIMER node with a valid duration_iso8601 starts an instance whose token reaches that node and arms exactly one timers row with status 'pending' and fire_at equal to the arrival timestamp plus the parsed duration -- replacing the {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :TIMER, _}} that transition.ex L294 returns today, asserted by a test that would have failed before this requirement
the timer row and the state-transition event are written in ONE transaction: a test that forces the event append to fail leaves NO timers row behind
when the timer fires, the instance advances along the TIMER node's outgoing edge and the token is no longer at the TIMER node

completing an instance sets every one of its PENDING timers to 'cancelled' with cancelled_at set, via the existing TaskActivation.cancel_pending_timers/2 call site in engine.ex -- which is still called from the same position inside the completion transaction (confirmed by git diff showing the call site itself unmoved)

cancelling an instance via Letflow.Engine.cancel_instance/3 likewise cancels its PENDING timers in the same transaction, and a test forcing that transaction to roll back leaves the timers still 'pending'

a timer whose status is already 'fired' is NOT changed by a subsequent instance cancellation (SCH-03's stated edge case), and no PENDING timer belonging to a CANCELLED or COMPLETED instance is ever fired by a later poll -- two explicit tests

lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex contains no Letflow.Repo call after this change, confirmed by the same grep its moduledoc already documents for purity, and the moduledoc names which return shape was extended to carry the timer-arming description instead
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: Independently re-verified all 10 acceptance-criteria groups (incl. REVIEWER's multi-timer-guard item) against the real code, not against prior reports. Read lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex in full, and the relevant sections of lib/letflow/engine.ex (prepare_timer_arms/4, build_timer_arms_multi/4, persist/11, advance_after_timer_fired/3, persist_timer_fired_advance/7, finalize_instance_projection/5, cancel_instance/3, run_cancel_instance/5), lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex's cancel_pending_timers/5, and lib/letflow/scheduler.ex's fire_timer/2/do_fire/2/attempt_fire/2. Confirmed via direct git diff read that AC4's cancel_pending_timers call site is unmoved (same position inside finalize_instance_projection/5's :completed clause, just given real args instead of the old no-op). Confirmed via direct source read that run_cancel_instance/5's :timer_cancellations Multi step genuinely sits between :open_tasks and :instance_projection (lines 2843-2867), matching the lock-ordering fix's claimed rationale exactly -- the single most fragile finding in this pipeline run, independently re-derived rather than trusted. Confirmed AC7's purity grep returns zero real matches (grep -n "Repo\.|Logger\.|DateTime\.|System\.os_time|System\.system_time|HTTPoison|Req\.|File\.|:rand\.|:crypto\." across instance_state.ex/token.ex/transition.ex hits only the moduledoc's own quoted grep-command text). Confirmed AC8 via git diff --stat main...HEAD: no lib/letflow_web/** or router file touched. Confirmed AC10 (multi-timer guard): prepare_timer_arms/4 returns a typed {:error, {:multiple_timers_in_one_hop_chain_not_supported, node_ids}} instead of proceeding to a Multi step-name collision that would raise; the dedicated regression test wraps the call in try/rescue and asserts no raise. Re-ran myself, blocking/foreground, not trusting TEST-RUNNER's run alone: mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean, 0 output); mix test on the 5 REQ-187-touched files (81 passed: 1 property, 80 tests -- exact match); the full suite via scripts/test_parallel.sh, 8 partitions (2552/2555 passed, 3 failures, all 3 in the documented pre-existing/environmental category -- 2x Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest rust-pin tests failing on rustc :enoent, no Rust toolchain in this sandbox, plus 1x Letflow.Engine.Wasm.PluginHandlerTest AC7 wasmex-Rust-NIF-source check; the previously-reported 4th failure, executor_test.exs's Lua wall-clock-timing flake, did not reproduce this run -- consistent with a timing flake, not a regression, and its absence proves nothing either way); mix format --check-formatted (exit 0, clean); mix letflow.lint_handoffs (OK, 0 new violations, 25 pre-existing grandfathered -- same count TEST-RUNNER reported).
